Definition: a reversal, i.e. the backside (of a gem), fold (of a double-leaved door), transmutation (of a name)
BiblicalUsage: Musabbah is a setting, a reversal, the back of a stone turned to show its face — the names of the sons of Israel are engraved on onyx stones, set in ouches of gold, and the rows of the breastplate are set in gold.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the setting is the honour: the names are not loose, they are set in gold and carried over the priest's heart.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
